title: Protocol for crystal structure determination of the antagonist-bound human cannabinoid receptor CB2
protocol: Thaw the cell pellets on ice.
Lyse the cells and suspend the cell pellet evenly with hypotonic buffer containing protease inhibitor (EDTA-Free, DMSO, BIMAKE).
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL homogenizer, place it on ice and grind it up and down 40–50 times.
Pour the solution into a 26 mL ultracentrifuge tube.
Wash the homogenizer with hypotonic buffer and transfer the liquid to the same centrifuge tube.
Balance the tubes and place them in a Beckman Optima XPN-90 ultracentrifuge with a Ti70 rotor.
Centrifuge at 40000 rpm for 30 min.
After centrifugation, discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell membrane pellet with 20 mL hypertonic buffer.
Transfer to the same homogenizer, place it on ice and grind for 40-50 times.
Put it into a centrifuge tube.
Wash with 5 mL hypertonic buffer.
After centrifugation, discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 2 mL cell membrane cryopreservation solution.
Grind it with a 2 mL homogenizer.
Suspend the cell membrane evenly in the cryopreservation solution.
Divide the cell membrane suspension evenly into two 2 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Quickly freeze with liquid nitrogen.
Store at -80°C for subsequent purification experiments.
Thaw the cell pellet on ice.
Lysate cells with 100 mL of hypotonic buffer containing protease inhibitor (Roche).
Transfer the cell suspension to a 100 mL homogenizer, place it on ice and grind up and down 40-50 times.
Pour the solution into two 70 mL ultracentrifuge tubes.
Wash the homogenizer with 30 mL hypotonic buffer and transfer it to centrifuge tube.
Balance the tubes.
Place in a Beckman Optima XPN-90 ultracentrifuge with a Ti45 rotor.
Centrifuge at 45000 rpm for 35 min.
After centrifugation, discard the supernatant.
Repeat steps ii–iv.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the washed membrane in hypertonic buffer and transfer to a homogenizer.
Place the homogenized mixture on ice.
Centrifuge the tubes using a Beckman Optima XPN-90 ultracentrifuge with a Ti45 rotor at 45000 rpm for 35 minutes.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation and repeat steps twice.
Resuspend the washed membrane uniformly in cryopreservation solution.
Split the membrane suspension evenly into two 50 ml tubes.
Freeze the tubes in liquid nitrogen and store them at -80°C.
Thaw the EP tube containing cell membrane suspension on ice.
Add 1× protease inhibitor, 2 mg/ml iodoacetamide, and 25 μM AM10257 (CB2 antagonist) to the thawed suspension.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 1 hour.
Add 1 mL 2× Solubilization Buffer and incubate at 4°C for 1–2 h.
Centrifuge at 14,000 rpm for 30 min after dissolving the membrane.
Transfer the supernatant into a 2 ml EP tube containing 50 μL TALON resin and 10 mM imidazole.
Bind for 12–16 hours at 4°C.
Take out the tube containing 25 mL of cell membrane suspension from -80°C and thaw it on ice.
Add 25 μM AM10257 and protease inhibitor (Roche) to the mixture.
Incubate at 4°C for 3 hours.
Add 2 mg/mL iodoacetamide and incubate at 4°C for 1 hour.
Add 25 mL of 2× Solubilization Buffer and incubate at 4°C for 2.5 hours.
Ultracentrifuge at 40,000 rpm for 30 min after dissolving the membrane.
Transfer the supernatant into a 50 ml tube containing 0.6 mL TALON resin and 10 mM imidazole.
Bind for 12–16 hours at 4°C.
Centrifuge the binding solution incubated 12–16 hours at 4°C at 800 g for 5 minutes.
Discard 1 mL of supernatant.
Transfer TALON resin to the rinsed small purification column.
Wash the protein with 20 column volumes of Wash buffer.
Elute the target protein with 4 column volumes of Elute buffer.
Centrifuge the binding solution incubated 12–16 hours at 4°C at 800 g for 5 minutes.
Discard 35 mL of supernatant.
Transfer TALON resin to the rinsed large purification column.
Wash the protein with 15 column volumes of Wash buffer 1.
Wash the protein with 15 column volumes of Wash buffer 2.
Elute the target protein with 3 column volumes of Elute buffer.
Concentrate the purified receptor to 18–25 mg/mL using a 100 kDa cut-off concentrator.
Transfer the concentrated protein to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Centrifuge at 14000 rpm for 30 minutes.
Use the concentrated protein for crystallization experiments.
Save a small amount of protein samples for protein property analysis.
Flush the column with ultrasonic degassed ddH2O at a flow rate of 0.2 mL/min for 1 hour.
Coat the column with BSA buffer (25 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 2% Glycerol, 0.03% LMNG, 0.01% CHS, 0.25 mg/mL BSA) at a flow rate of 0.2 mL/min for ≥4 hours.
Equilibrate the column and system with HPLC buffer (25 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 500 mM NaCl, 2% Glycerol, 0.03% LMNG, 0.01% CHS) at a flow rate of 0.5 mL/min for 2–3 hours.
Centrifuge the CB2-T4L sample at 14000 rpm for 10 minutes.
Load the centrifuged sample into the HPLC for analysis.
Dissolve CPM dye powder in DMSO at a concentration of 4 mg/mL.
Store the dissolved CPM dye at -80°C in the dark.
Dilute the stored CPM dye 1:20 with elution buffer without imidazole.
Mix 0.5 μL of the diluted CPM dye with about 1 μg of CB2-T4L protein solution to a final volume of 50 μL.
Incubate the mixture for 15 minutes in the dark at 20°C.
Mix lipid and cholesterol to prepare a lipid-cholesterol mixture.
Allow the grease to reach 20°C before use.
Take the Eppendorf tube and place it in a real-time PCR instrument (QIAGEN Rotor-Gene Q).
Set the excitation light wavelength to 387 nm.
Set the emission light wavelength to 463 nm.
Set the temperature range for detecting fluorescence from 20°C to 90°C.
Use GraphPad Prism software for data analysis.
Select constructs with relatively higher Tm values based on fluorescence thermal stability experiment results.
Choose protein constructs or ligands with Tm values higher than 60°C for further crystallization trials.
Weigh monoolein and cholesterol in a 4 mL brown bottle according to the mass ratio of 9:1.
Add chloroform dropwise until powder is completely dissolved.
Use nitrogen flow to volatilize chloroform until solution becomes transparent and viscous.
Seal with aluminum foil, leave a vent with a syringe needle, and place in a vacuum container.
Keep container under vacuum for about 24 hours to ensure complete evaporation of chloroform.
Take out sample, tighten cap and seal with Parafilm, then store at -20°C for future use.
Wash two 100 μL Hamilton Syringes with methanol and dry them before use.
Heat Lipid-Cholesterol mixture at 42°C to dissolve grease.
Centrifuge protein sample (CB2-T4L) at 14,000 rpm.
Transfer protein solution weight-determined protein to one of the preheated 100 μL Syringes using a thin pipette tip to avoid bubbles.
According to the weight ratio of 2 (Protein): 3 (Lipid), transfer prepared lipid to another 100 μL Syringe preheated at 42°C.
Mix two Syringes using the coupler.
Place the connected syringes at 20°C.
Mix the contents of the syringes slowly for 1 second in a back-and-forth motion to form a transparent LCP phase.
Follow the instructions provided by the crystallization robot, Formulatrix NT8, for high-throughput crystallization screening.
Include pH values of 5.0, 6.0, 7.0, and 8.0 in the preliminary screening conditions.
Use Hampton Salts with concentrations of 100 mM and 400 mM, including 49 unique salts, for the screening.
Test PEG400 concentrations ranging from 25% to 40% during the preliminary screening.
Utilize commercial membrane protein crystallization kits as part of the screening process.
